[0] [0] Apple is about to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, and a new report suggests its price may not be as steep as some analysts have suggested. Here's what you need to know.

[1] [1] iPhone 18 Pro could see just a $100 price hike, following similar pricing strategies from Samsung and Google

[2] [2] Apple is set to hold an event where it will officially unveil its flagship iPhone 18 Pro, with details of the September event expected to be announced next week.

[3] [3] While we already know quite a bit about the iPhone 18 Pro, including rumored camera upgrades and design changes, the pricing remains a major question mark.

[4] [4] Given the rising component costs for memory, storage, and the all-new camera system, analysts have predicted the iPhone 18 Pro will start at $1,299 or $1,399 for the base model alone.

[5] [5] However, the final price may not be that extreme. Mark Gurman writes for Bloomberg:

[6] [6] The company has been watching how Samsung and Google have handled rising component costs. Both companies raised prices on their latest phones by around $100. If Apple follows a similar increase, the iPhone 18 Pro would be priced at $1,199, representing roughly a 9% increase. Given how severe the memory shortage is, that's a fairly modest bump and shows Apple is absorbing some of the added costs itself. The company has warned of margin pressure this quarter—a sign that it isn't passing all of its rising expenses onto consumers. �果There is reason to not push the increase too high. A $100 bump keeps the iPhone broadly within Samsung's pricing range, avoiding the sticker shock seen with some of the bigger hikes on the Mac and iPad.

[7] [9] A $100 increase would see the iPhone 18 Pro go from $1,099 to $1,199, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max rise from $1,199 to $1,299.

[8] [10] Earlier reports suggested Apple might reserve larger price hikes for higher storage tiers. If the company does keep the entry-level 256GB model's increase to $100, we could still see 512GB, 1TB, and above models increase by $150 or $200.

[9] [11] What do you think the iPhone 18 Pro will be priced at? Let us know in the comments.
